dedupe_keys.name: high resolution surface faulting from the 1983 idaho lost river fault mw 6 9 earthquake and previous events

description: High-resolution surface faulting from the 1983 Idaho Lost River Fault Mw 6.9 earthquake and previous events is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Simone Bello et al. We present high-resolution mapping and surface faulting measurements along the Lost River fault (Idaho-USA), a normal fault activated in the 1983 (Mw 6.9) earthquake. The earthquake ruptured ~35 km of the fault with a maximum throw of ~3 m. Coverage: national (US); published in 2021. Formats: GeoTIFF, Shapefile, MATLAB, TXT, Image. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 6935 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
